_about: Claude's analysis for the Opportunities page (pipeline/website.py opportunities), in ranked order. Each entry says what became free, who would buy it, why now, and what to check. Written from each patent's abstract and claims; market context is general, with no figures.

US-8551104-B2.open: A cordless, hand-held diode-laser device for slowing hair regrowth, with its battery-driven pulse circuit inside the housing.
US-8551104-B2.buyers: At-home beauty device brands and salons that want a cordless laser rather than a flash lamp.
US-8551104-B2.now: Diode lasers and high-drain lithium cells are far cheaper than in 2006, and at-home light-based hair removal is an established consumer category.
US-8551104-B2.watch: Laser devices sold for this use need FDA clearance and eye-safety engineering, and the original owner may hold newer patents.

US-8766483-B2.open: Extending wireless charging range by having a second, differently sized resonant antenna pick up power and re-transmit it to a nearby device.
US-8766483-B2.buyers: Makers of desks, car consoles, shelves and IoT hubs that want charging to reach farther than one pad.
US-8766483-B2.now: Phones, earbuds and sensors all charge wirelessly now, and people want charging surfaces rather than exact placement.
US-8766483-B2.watch: Wireless power is crowded with newer patents, so check freedom to operate for the specific antenna design you use.

US-8787621-B2.open: Estimating an animal's weight from a camera image by matching it to models of known weight, then tracking daily gain and forecasting weight.
US-8787621-B2.buyers: Ranches, feedlots, dairies and livestock auctions that weigh animals by hand or on scales.
US-8787621-B2.now: Phone cameras and off-the-shelf vision models make this a software product rather than a research project.
US-8787621-B2.watch: The owner's related applications may still be alive; check the family before launching.

US-8788096-B1.open: A two-wheeled self-balancing telepresence robot with a camera head on a slim telescoping shaft and a stabilizer that retracts into the base.
US-8788096-B1.buyers: Remote-work offices, hospitals, eldercare homes and building security.
US-8788096-B1.now: Hoverboard-style motors, cheap IMUs and video calling have made balancing robots inexpensive to build.
US-8788096-B1.watch: Other telepresence robot patents remain in force, so keep to the claimed layout or check them.

US-8706742-B1.open: Ranking documents for relevance to an issue, then mining their metadata (senders, dates, folders) for leads that correlate with the high scores.
US-8706742-B1.buyers: Law firms, e-discovery vendors and compliance teams reviewing large document sets.
US-8706742-B1.now: Language models make document scoring cheap, and the metadata-lead step adds an explainable layer on top.
US-8706742-B1.watch: E-discovery has many active patents; the claims here are specific to the iterative control-subset method.

US-8634686-B2.open: A solar concentrator that tracks the sun with no motors: two immiscible fluids move toward the hot spot and couple focused light into a light guide.
US-8634686-B2.buyers: Solar and daylighting companies looking for flat, trackerless concentrators.
US-8634686-B2.now: Cheap high-efficiency cells and interest in low-maintenance solar make passive tracking more attractive.
US-8634686-B2.watch: This is lab-grade optics; expect real materials and lifetime testing before a product.

US-8577630-B2.open: When a battery pack detects a failure, a latch automatically drains its stored energy so a damaged pack holds less charge.
US-8577630-B2.buyers: E-bike, e-scooter, power-tool and home battery makers, and fleet operators.
US-8577630-B2.now: Battery fires in micromobility are a public concern, and the claim is broad: detect, latch, drain.
US-8577630-B2.watch: Draining a damaged lithium pack safely takes careful thermal design and testing to UL standards.

US-8641415-B2.open: Finding cracks in a tooth, even under a crown, by stressing it gently and listening to its acoustic emission against a baseline recorded earlier.
US-8641415-B2.buyers: Dental device makers and dental practices.
US-8641415-B2.now: Small piezo sensors and signal-processing chips are cheap, and cracked teeth are hard to find with X-rays.
US-8641415-B2.watch: A diagnostic dental device needs regulatory clearance before sale.

US-8593286-B2.open: Wireless body sensors feeding a system that gives athletes statistical feedback and a coaching instruction for a defined sport.
US-8593286-B2.buyers: Sports-tech startups, coaching apps, teams and training academies.
US-8593286-B2.now: Watches and clip-on motion sensors are everywhere; the value is in sport-specific feedback.
US-8593286-B2.watch: Sports analytics is crowded, so keep the build close to the claimed rules-based feedback.

US-8745998-B2.open: Predicting when fog has formed on a vehicle window and switching the defroster on and off automatically.
US-8745998-B2.buyers: Electric vehicle makers, bus and truck fleets, and aftermarket climate-control suppliers.
US-8745998-B2.now: In electric vehicles cabin heating costs driving range, so running the defroster only when needed saves energy.
US-8745998-B2.watch: Automakers hold many newer climate-control patents; check the sensors you plan to use.

US-8794601-B2.open: A humidifier that uses furnace condensate, passing water through a membrane that blocks the condensate's acid, with airflow across it.
US-8794601-B2.now: Condensing furnaces are standard and already produce the water; the claim has just two elements, so it is broad.
US-8794601-B2.watch: Membrane choice, water quality and local plumbing codes need checking.

US-8682482-B2.open: A robot arm that watches a worker, estimates how far along a task they are, and hands over the next part at the right moment.
US-8682482-B2.buyers: Small manufacturers, repair shops, labs and commercial kitchens.
US-8682482-B2.now: Camera-based pose tracking and low-cost collaborative arms make this practical outside big factories.
US-8682482-B2.watch: Collaborative robots must meet safety standards for working near people.

US-8678771-B2.open: Building metal parts from a stack of bonded foils cut from slices of a 3D model, where the foils differ in thickness.
US-8678771-B2.buyers: Makers of heat exchangers, cooling plates, tooling and aerospace parts.
US-8678771-B2.now: Laser and waterjet cutting are cheap, and laminated metal parts can be made without a metal 3D printer.
US-8678771-B2.watch: Bond strength and flatness decide whether parts pass; plan testing early.

US-8660842-B2.open: Using a camera to judge a room's shape, then tuning echo and noise removal before recognizing speech.
US-8660842-B2.buyers: Video-conferencing hardware, smart speakers with cameras, cars and home robots.
US-8660842-B2.now: Devices with both a camera and microphones are common, and vision models can read a room's layout.
US-8660842-B2.watch: Speech processing has many active patents; the claim needs the image-to-reverberation step.

US-8773052-B2.open: Driving a brushless motor with a phase advance that varies periodically over time and adjusts with motor speed.
US-8773052-B2.buyers: Makers of vacuums, fans, drones, power tools and e-bike motor controllers.
US-8773052-B2.now: Brushless motors are in almost everything with a fan or wheel, and this is firmware on a cheap microcontroller.
US-8773052-B2.watch: The motor maker may hold newer control patents; implement the claimed method, not later refinements.

US-8658106-B2.open: A cover for a fuel pump handle that sprays sanitizer on the handle after it is put back.
US-8658106-B2.buyers: Fuel station chains, EV charging networks and pump makers.
US-8658106-B2.now: People expect cleaner shared touch points, and EV charging cables have the same problem.
US-8658106-B2.watch: Sanitizer spraying at a fuel pump has fire-safety and chemical rules to meet.

US-8590533-B2.open: A hands-free breathing-resistance training mask with interchangeable inlet plugs that set how hard it is to inhale.
US-8590533-B2.buyers: Fitness brands, sports teams and respiratory-training coaches.
US-8590533-B2.now: Breathing training is a growing fitness niche, and the mask can be made by injection molding.
US-8590533-B2.watch: Health claims for breathing devices are regulated; sell it as training equipment.

US-8747287-B2.open: A chair whose back pivots against swappable spring cylinders, so sitting doubles as a back-extension exercise.
US-8747287-B2.buyers: Office furniture makers and home-fitness brands.
US-8747287-B2.now: Desk work and back pain are common, and people want exercise built into furniture.
US-8747287-B2.watch: Load testing for furniture safety standards is required.
